summary: Weighted route migration triggered runtime thread softlock causing sustained 5xx floor for tenant
description:
Issue summary: After a scheduled weighted-route migration (traffic shift) for a set of dedicated tenants in us-east-1, a single tenant (LexiconAI) observed a persistent elevated 5xx error rate (~12% of requests) for ~90 minutes. Impact: customer-facing API requests returned 502/503/504, streaming sessions dropped, and tail latency increased. Scope: observed across a 6-instance serving pool behind the same route weight group; not global.

Initial detection: LexiconAI support pinged #support at 2026-03-13T20:02Z noting a spike in 5xx and customer-facing errors. Alerting (apigw 5xx-rate) fired at ~20:01Z.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Trigger a weighted route migration that shifts ~30% of traffic from route A to route B for the us-east serving pool.
2) Observe increase in concurrent connection churn to runtime processes during in-flight model cache lookups.
3) Note repeated runtime thread stalls and watchdog restarts corresponding with API 5xx spikes.
4) Reproduce by replaying a 10-minute sample trace of LexiconAI traffic through canary routing (captured request IDs attached).
logs: apigw: 2026-03-13T20:01:12Z - 502 upstream reset; runtime: 2026-03-13T20:01:13Z - ThreadPoolWorker[7] softlock detected at kv_cache.c:742; 2026-03-13T20:01:17Z - watchdog initiated graceful restart; container restart count incremented; dmesg shows no OOM; kernel logs show high scheduler wait times; network proxies returned ECONNRESET patterns during route handover.
investigation_notes: Support triaged and validated customer impact; secured customer permission to triage live logs.
SRE observed runtime thread 'softlock' where workers spin waiting on a prefix-cache lock while new prefetch requests flood during migration.
Heap/CPU profiles show high user CPU from kernel-optimized attention kernels on 4/6 instances; one instance showed thread starvation with backlog growth in per-worker queue.
Autoscaler did not spin up additional dedicated instances because the route weight change occurred within the same instance pool and the autoscaler threshold was not breached.

Correlation between route-migration window and initial 5xx surge is strong; hypothesis: migration produced concentrated prefetch hotspots and lock contention on KV cache leading to per-runtime backpressure and upstream 502/503s.
comments: 2026-03-13T20:08Z - Diego Marquez (assignee): 'We're seeing repeated worker softlocks on two runtimes. Temporarily shifted LexiconAI traffic off the affected route to mitigate impact.'
2026-03-13T20:22Z - SRE: 'Mitigation in place — decreased weight to the failing route by 40% and bounced runtimes on the two offenders. Error rate dropped to ~1.2%.'
2026-03-13T21:10Z - Customer (LexiconAI): 'Thanks — we saw immediate improvement after your weight rollback. Please advise on root cause and long-term fix.'
2026-03-14T02:05Z - Runtime eng: 'Reproduced softlock locally with traffic-replay and a crafted prefetch burst; identified lock-order inversion when prefetch and eviction run concurrently.'
actions_taken: 1) Emergency mitigation: partially rolled back weighted-route change for LexiconAI and diverted traffic to healthy pool. 2) Restarted two affected runtime containers and monitored for recovery. 3) Enabled additional request queue headroom for the tenant to reduce prefetch pressure. 4) Created a canary job to replay customer traffic to replicate state. 5) Notified customer and provided status updates.
resolution: Partial fix applied: rollback of weight migration + runtime restarts restored normal 5xx baseline. Root cause under active investigation (lock-order inversion in prefix/KV prefetch + eviction path). No data loss; customer satisfied with mitigation.
follow_up_actions: 1) Runtime team to land PR that adds finer-grained cache locking and avoids global prefetch stall (PR referenced above).
2) Add route-migration throttling to limit concurrent prefetches across a pool (runbook task).
3) Update autoscaler thresholds for routing-induced prefetch hotspots so dedicated pool can scale proactively.
4) Postmortem and Confluence runbook update with clear mitigation steps and 'when to rollback' guidance.
5) Schedule 1:1 with LexiconAI CSM to review impact and SLA credits if requested.
